title: Chapter 9. Yukta-vairagya
html:
Sanatana's question about "yukta-vairagya"; two kinds of renunciation — "phalgu" (empty) and "yukta" (fitting); how renunciant and householder should live: accept what is necessary without attachment, serve Krishna and the Vaishnavas according to one's means (pp. 24–27)

[p. 24]

1One day Gosai Sanatana asked:
"What is called yukta-vairagya? Describe it, Lord.

2The Mayavadis say all is like crow's dung;
the sannyasi who sees the world of the senses [so] is the highest.

3What befits a Vaishnava — I wish to know;
mercifully command me; I will take the command on my head."

4The Lord says: "Renunciation is of two kinds:
the difference between 'phalgu' and 'yukta' I have explained again and again.1

5When karmis and jnanis take refuge in disgust with the world,
phalgu-vairagya with evil intent arises in their hearts.

[p. 25]

6Then contempt for the world comes to them,
and they take up a dharma that is merely the opposite of matter.

7Service to Krishna, service to sadhus, the tasting of the soul's rasa
fall into utter decline in a dharma that is merely the opposite of matter.

8The mind of the phalgu-vairagi is always dry, devoid of rasa:
the name, form, qualities and lila are not to his liking.

9For the yukta-vairagi devotion is easily attained:
all that he uses is sanctified by devotion to Krishna.

10His mind easily leaves the dull qualities of nature
and, taking refuge in spirit, quickly plunges into the transcendent rasa of bhakti.

11By bhakti-yoga he gains Sri Krishna's favour:
"My devotee never perishes" — so His vow proclaims.2

12He to whom Krishna, pleased, shows mercy —
he is blessed in this world.

13The highest feeling of Goloka shines in his heart:
in Gokula he attains Goloka, and maya falls far away.3

14O brother, cast off dry renunciation now,
accept yukta-vairagya and always hold it in your heart.

15Leaving all worldly things, brother, tell me, where will you go?
Go to the forest — and there too is the tangle of worldly affairs.

[p. 26]

16Your stomach will go with you; how much trouble there will be
to keep the body going — think it over.

17Without reason life will quickly waste away;
and if you die — how then will you conquer maya?

18And if you do not die, you will grow weak;
when the mind fails, where is the place for knowledge?

19Sitting at home, always taking Krishna's name,
use what is fitting without attachment.4

20Grasp the inner sense of the word "fitting",
lest, taking a crooked meaning, you become a pleaser of the body.

21Accept what is favourable to pure devotion;
reject what is unfavourable to it.

22Whoever, abandoning the inner meaning, takes the words literally,
pleasing the body, in the grip of taste, takes a crooked path:

23he eats well, dresses well, amasses wealth,
and passes day and night addicted to the company of women.

24The foolish seek a soft bed and mansions.
What is truly needed and suited to maintaining the body —
accept such things and maintain the body.

25Eat sattvic food, avoid intoxicants;
with compassion for all beings perform loud sankirtana.

[p. 27]

26On the pretext of serving the Deity do not hoard worldly things;
always avoid attachment and aversion to worldly things.

27Violence, deceit, enmity with others —
never allow them, brother, if you hold to my word.

28In solitude discuss pure devotion;
pass your days linking them to Krishna's service.

29Do not strive for mathas, temples, halls and houses;
if you have wealth, brother, do as you wish.5

30If you have no wealth, then only simple, sattvic service:
offering water and tulasi, hold Giridhari to your breast.

31Weeping with feeling, say: "I am Yours;
may Your lotus feet abide in my heart."

32Honour the Vaishnavas by offering them prasada and the like;
if you have no wealth, please them with humble words and entreaty.

33Family and dependants are Krishna's servants and maidservants:
caring for them as for yourself, be sweet in speech.

34Remembrance, kirtana, service, compassion for all beings —
this is what you will do, having become a yukta-vairagi.

35If Krishna gives no family and dependants
or, having given, takes them away — He is the mine of all happiness:

36give up grief and delusion, brother, chant the Name unceasingly."
Jagai says: "Over this I have had many a quarrel with Gaura."6

Notes

  1. Phalgu-vairagya — "empty" renunciation that rejects even what is connected with Krishna; yukta-vairagya — "fitting" renunciation: using everything without attachment, in connection with Krishna (Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu 1.2.255–256). In the CC the Lord gives the instruction on yukta-vairagya to Raghunatha Dasa (Madhya 16.238); Sanatana's question is known only from the Prema-vivarta.
  2. Gita 9.31.
  3. That is, Goloka, Krishna's spiritual abode, is revealed already here, in Gokula (the earthly Vraja).
  4. Cf. CC Madhya 16.238.
  5. That is, building is not an end in itself; where there are means, service may take this form too. Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati, who founded mathas and temples, regarded them as means of service and preaching, not as worldly acquisition.
  6. Cf. CC Antya 12–13: Jagadananda argues with the Lord, unwilling to see His severe austerities.
